summary: This note describes the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), created under the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988. It explains the authority's statutory function under Section 16(1), its formal start of operations in February 1995 as an autonomous body, and its responsibilities for national highways and toll collection. It also names Yogendra Narain as the first Chairman.
one_line: NHAI, created by the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988, develops and manages India's national highways and collects tolls.
key_facts: The National Highways Authority of India was created through the promulgation of the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988.

Section 16(1) of the National Highways Authority of India Act states that the function of NHAI is to develop, maintain and manage the national highways and any other highways vested in, or entrusted to, it by the Government of India.
NHAI came into operations in February 1995 and was formally made an autonomous body.
NHAI is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways.
National Highways under NHAI's responsibility total over 92,851.05 km (57,694.97 mi) in length.
NHAI is also responsible for toll collection on several highways.
Yogendra Narain was the first Chairman of NHAI in 1988.
Yogendra Narain is a retired IAS officer of Uttar Pradesh cadre.
